key_insight: MCL-PINNs is a phase-field neural solver that combines discrete-time PINNs with specialized training tricks to reliably capture moving contact lines and sharp interface evolution under dynamic boundary conditions.
engineering_relevance: It offers a mesh-free, physics-informed tool for simulating wetting, coalescence, and droplet deformation in interfacial fluid systems where standard PINNs struggle.
method: Multi-network time marching to reduce long-time error accumulation
Relaxed output distribution constraints and variable scaling for sharp phase-field features
Adaptive loss weighting plus interface-focused collocation sampling; symmetry inputs when applicable
evidence_signal: The method is validated on three numerical cases—droplet coalescence, shear-induced droplet deformation, and dynamic wetting in a heterogeneous channel—and is reported to outperform standard PINN formulations.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful tuning of scaling, adaptive sampling, and loss weights, especially for highly localized contact-line dynamics.
paper_title: A phase-field neural solver for moving contact line problems with dynamic boundary conditions
